title: observability: add token-level + KV cache metrics, tracing, logging and dashboards with alert tuning
author: Ravi Srinivasan
release_notes: Add token-level cost/latency + KV cache metrics; new observability dashboard and tuned alerts. Backwards-compatible metrics names; no breaking API changes.
description:
Context: Production teams asked for finer-grained observability into per-request token cost/latency, and better visibility into KV-cache behaviour for us to reduce token egress and improve routing decisions. This PR implements token-level metrics, KV cache metrics, tracing span enrichments, structured logging fields for correlation IDs, a Grafana dashboard, and initial alert tuning.

What this changes (high level):
- Export token-level metrics (redwood_inference_tokens_generated, redwood_inference_token_latency_ms) with labels: model, route, customer_tier, outcome (cache_hit/cache_miss).
- Add KV cache metrics (redwood_kv_cache_hits, redwood_kv_cache_misses, redwood_kv_cache_evictions, redwood_kv_cache_hit_latency_ms) and expose per-shard stats.
- Enrich OTEL traces with span attributes: token_count, kv_cache_hit (bool), kv_key_ids (hashed), and route_id.
- Structured logs: include request_id, trace_id, token_count, kv_hit=true/false, and auth_tier. Logs are JSON-encoded by default in prod.
- Grafana: new dashboard (Observability / Token & KV metrics) with panels for token cost/latency breakdowns, KV hit-rate heatmap, trace waterfall samples, and alerting rules.
- Alert tuning: adjusted thresholds for token-latency P95/P99, KV-miss-rate alerts, and a new composite alert that fires only when high token-cost and high KV-miss-rate coincide for 10m.

Checklist:
- [x] Metrics exported with Prometheus-friendly names and help text
- [x] OTEL span attributes added and covered by integration test harness
- [x] Structured logging updated with correlation fields
- [x] Grafana dashboard JSON + provisioning added
- [x] Unit & integration tests updated
- [x] Alert thresholds reviewed with SRE and adjusted

Commits (summary):
- add: token-level metrics exporter and unit tests
- feat: kv cache metrics + per-shard stats and tests
- perf: batch metrics emission and reduce cardinality for model/route labels
- feat: trace enrichment + span unit tests
- feat: structured logging fields and formatter
- docs: dashboard README + alert rationale

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/observability/metrics/token_metrics.go (new)
- pkg/observability/metrics/kv_metrics.go (new)
- pkg/observability/tracing/span_enricher.go (modified)
- pkg/observability/logging/json_formatter.go (modified)
- infra/grafana/dashboards/token_kv_dashboard.json (new)
- infra/alerts/token_kv_alerts.yaml (new)
- internal/e2e/observability_integration_test.go (modified)
- docs/observability/token-kv-dashboard.md (new)

Notes on implementation decisions:
- To limit cardinality we hash KV keys and only emit kv_key_bucket label (256 buckets) instead of full keys. The README explains the bucket scheme and how to correlate back using trace spans.
- Token metrics are emitted at request completion; we considered streaming token metrics but the perf cost was too high. We added a low-overhead sampling mode (1%) in the config for high-volume clients.
- Alerts use a composite rule so teams aren't paged on transient increases in token latency when the KV hit-rate is healthy. SRE recommended 10m sustained window.

Migration and backward compatibility:
- Metric names and help text follow existing naming. No removal of old metrics; all new metrics are additive.

Testing & CI:
- Unit tests for metrics helpers and formatting.
- Integration test spins up the metrics exporter + Prometheus scrape target and verifies a KV hit/miss scenario emits expected metrics.
- Perf-canary run showed <1% overhead on tail latency with metrics enabled (sampling off).

Follow-ups:
- Add dashboard panels for model-quantization breakdown and per-customer cost. (ENG-7890)
- Add automated rollup job to compute per-route daily token cost and store in long-term metrics index.

Related: ENG-7821, SUP-452, ENG-7890
